title.zh: 卷七十五 晉書1: 高祖本紀一
title.en: Volume 75 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1
title.raw: 卷七十五 晉書1: 高祖本紀一 Volume 75 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝，姓石氏，諱敬瑭，太原人也。

translations.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, bore the surname Shi and the taboo name Jingtang; he was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, honored as the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, belonged to the Shi clan; his personal name was Jingtang, and he came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 本衛大夫碏、漢丞相奮之後，漢衰，關輔亂，子孫流泛西裔，故有居甘州者焉。

translations.literal: Originally he was descended from Wei grandee Que and Han chancellor Fen; when Han declined and the capital region fell into turmoil, descendants drifted westward, and hence some came to dwell in Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His lineage traced back to Que, a grandee of Wei, and Fen, a chancellor of Han. After the Han dynasty waned and the Guanfu region was thrown into chaos, his forebears were scattered toward the western frontier, and some of them settled in Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 四代祖璟，以唐元和中與沙陀軍都督朱耶氏自靈武入附，憲宗嘉之，隸為河東陰山府裨校，以邊功累官至朔州刺史。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Jing, in the Yuanhe era of Tang together with the Shatuo military commissioner Zhu Ye's clan came from Lingwu to submit; Emperor Xianzong commended this, enrolled him as a deputy commander of the Hedong Yinshan command, and through border achievements rose in succession to prefect of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Jing, during the Yuanhe reign of Tang, entered imperial allegiance from Lingwu together with the Zhu Ye clan, chieftains of the Shatuo army. Emperor Xianzong praised the submission and enrolled Jing as a deputy commander in the Hedong Yinshan command. Through repeated achievements on the frontier he rose step by step to military governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，追尊為孝安皇帝，廟號靖祖，陵曰義陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiao'an, with temple name Jingzu and tomb called Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu he was posthumously ennobled as Emperor Xiao'an, with the temple name Jingzu and the tomb named Yiling.

sentences.zh: 祖妣秦氏，追謚為孝安元皇后。

translations.literal: His paternal grandmother, née Qin, was posthumously given the title Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal grandmother, Lady Qin, was posthumously honored as Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.

sentences.zh: 三代祖郴，早薨，贈左散騎常侍，追尊為孝簡皇帝，廟號肅祖，陵曰惠陵。

translations.literal: His third-generation ancestor Chen died young; he was posthumously given the office of Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and honored as Emperor Xiao Jian, with temple name Suzu and tomb called Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: His third-generation ancestor Chen died in early life and was posthumously appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry. Later he was ennobled as Emperor Xiao Jian, with the temple name Suzu and the tomb named Huiling.

sentences.zh: 祖妣安氏，追謚孝簡恭皇后。

translations.literal: His paternal grandmother, née An, was posthumously given the title Empress Gong of Xiao Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal grandmother, Lady An, was posthumously honored as Empress Gong of Xiao Jian.

sentences.zh: 皇祖諱翌，任振武防禦使，贈尚書右僕射，追尊孝平皇帝，廟號睿祖，陵曰康陵。

translations.literal: His imperial grandfather, taboo name Yi, served as defense commissioner of Zhenwu; he was posthumously given the office of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and honored as Emperor Xiao Ping, with temple name Ruizu and tomb called Kangling.
translations.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather Yi had served as defense commissioner of Zhenwu and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. He was later ennobled as Emperor Xiao Ping, with the temple name Ruizu and the tomb named Kangling.

sentences.zh: 祖妣米氏，追謚孝平獻皇后。

translations.literal: His paternal grandmother, née Mi, was posthumously given the title Empress Xian of Xiao Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal grandmother, Lady Mi, was posthumously honored as Empress Xian of Xiao Ping.

sentences.zh: 皇考諱紹雍，番字臬捩雞，善騎射，有經遠大略，事後唐武皇及莊宗，累立戰功，與周德威相亞，歷平、洺二州刺史，薨於任，贈太傅，追尊為孝元皇帝，廟號憲祖，陵曰昌陵。

translations.literal: His imperial father, taboo name Shaoyong, had the tribal name Nielexiji; he excelled at mounted archery and possessed far-reaching strategic vision. He served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong, repeatedly winning battle honors, ranking second only to Zhou Dewei, and served as prefect of Ping and Mo; he died in office and was posthumously given Grand Tutor, honored as Emperor Xiao Yuan, with temple name Xianzu and tomb called Changling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaoyong, known in the tribal tongue as Nielexiji, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and possessed a statesman's long view. He served both the Martial Emperor of Later Tang and Emperor Zhuangzong, winning repeated honors in battle and standing second only to Zhou Dewei. He held the prefectures of Ping and Mo, died in office, and was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor. He was later ennobled as Emperor Xiao Yuan, with the temple name Xianzu and the tomb named Changling.

sentences.zh: 皇妣何氏，追謚孝元懿皇后。

translations.literal: His imperial mother, née He, was posthumously given the title Empress Yi of Xiao Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady He, was posthumously honored as Empress Yi of Xiao Yuan.

sentences.zh: 帝即孝元之第二子也，以唐景福元年二月二十八日生於太原汾陽裏，時有白氣充庭，人甚異焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor was the second son of Xiao Yuan; he was born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jingfu of Tang in Fenyang Lane, Taiyuan; at that time white vapor filled the courtyard, and people were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was the second son of Xiao Yuan. He was born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jingfu at Fenyang Lane in Taiyuan. A white mist filled the courtyard at his birth, and those present were deeply struck by the omen.

sentences.zh: 及長，性沈淡，寡言笑，讀兵法，重李牧、周亞夫行事。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his nature was calm and restrained; he spoke little and laughed rarely; he studied military treatises and esteemed the conduct of Li Mu and Zhou Yafu.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he grew reserved and quiet, seldom given to speech or laughter. He studied military strategy and took Li Mu and Zhou Yafu as his models.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗為代州刺史，每深心器之，因妻以愛女。

translations.literal: When Tang's Emperor Mingzong was prefect of Daizhou, he always held the Emperor in deep regard and therefore gave him his beloved daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Daizhou, the future Emperor Mingzong of Tang came to esteem him deeply and gave him his beloved daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗聞其善射，擢居左右，明宗請隸大軍，從之。

translations.literal: Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong heard of his skill in archery and promoted him to his personal guard; Mingzong requested that he be assigned to the main army, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang heard of his marksmanship, he took him into his personal guard. Mingzong then asked that he be assigned to the main army, and Zhuangzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 後明宗從莊宗征行，命帝領親騎，號「三討軍」，倚以心腹。

translations.literal: Later, when Mingzong followed Zhuangzong on campaign, he ordered the Emperor to lead the personal cavalry, called the "Three Campaigns Army," and relied on him as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Mingzong accompanied Zhuangzong on campaign, he put the emperor in command of the personal cavalry, known as the "Three Campaigns Army," and treated him as one of his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 天祐十二年，莊宗並有河北之地，開府於鄴，梁遣上將劉鄩以兵五萬營於莘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong united the Hebei region and established his headquarters at Ye; Liang sent its senior general Liu Yan with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong brought all of Hebei under his control and opened his headquarters at Ye. Liang dispatched its senior general Liu Yan with fifty thousand men to encamp at Xin.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，鄩引兵突至清平，薄於城下。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Yan led his troops in a sudden advance to Qingping and pressed close beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, Yan drove his army in a sudden thrust to Qingping and pressed up against the city walls.

sentences.zh: 莊宗至自甘陵，兵未陣，多為鄩所掩。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong arrived from Ganling, but before his troops could form ranks, many were overrun by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong arrived from Ganling, but before his troops could form their lines, many were caught and overrun by Yan's forces.

sentences.zh: 帝領十餘騎，橫槊深入，東西馳突，無敢當者，卒全部伍而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor led a dozen horsemen, spear held crosswise, plunging deep; he charged east and west, and none dared oppose him; he finally gathered the whole unit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led a dozen horsemen deep into the enemy ranks with his spear held crosswise, charging back and forth until no one dared stand against him. At last he gathered his whole unit and brought them safely back.

sentences.zh: 莊宗壯之，拊其背曰：「將門出將，言不謬爾。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong admired his valor, clapped him on the back, and said, "A general's house produces a general—the saying is not mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was impressed by his courage, clapped him on the back, and said, "A general's house breeds a general—the old saying is true of you."

sentences.zh: 」因頒以器帛，復親為啖酥，當時以為異恩，由是知名。

translations.literal: He then bestowed vessels and silks upon him and personally fed him butter; at the time this was regarded as extraordinary favor, and from this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded him with vessels and silks and personally fed him butter with his own hand. At the time this was regarded as an extraordinary honor, and from that moment his name became widely known.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄩兵陣於莘之西北，明宗從莊宗酣戰。

translations.literal: The next year, Yan's army formed battle lines northwest of Xin; Mingzong followed Zhuangzong in fierce combat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yan drew up his army northwest of Xin, and Mingzong fought at Zhuangzong's side in a bitter engagement.

sentences.zh: 久之，塵埃四合，帝與明宗俱陷陣內，帝挺身躍劍，反復轉鬥，行數十里，逐鄩於故元城之東。

translations.literal: After a long while dust closed in from all sides; the Emperor and Mingzong were both trapped within the enemy formation; the Emperor threw himself forward, leaping with his sword, fighting back and forth repeatedly for several tens of li, and drove Yan east of the old Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while dust closed in on every side, and both the emperor and Mingzong were trapped inside the enemy formation. The emperor threw himself forward, sword in hand, fighting back and forth for miles until he had driven Yan east of the old Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 是日，鄩軍殺傷過半。

translations.literal: On that day more than half of Yan's army was killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: That day more than half of Yan's army was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 十五年，唐軍拔楊劉鎮，梁將賀瑰設伏於無石山，明宗為瑰所迫，帝為後殿，破梁軍五百餘騎，按轡而還。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Tang army captured Yangliu Fort; Liang's general He Gui set an ambush at Wushi Mountain; Mingzong was pressed by Gui; the Emperor served as rearguard, broke more than five hundred Liang horsemen, and returned at an easy pace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Tang army took Yangliu Fort. Liang's general He Gui laid an ambush at Wushi Mountain and pressed Mingzong hard. The emperor covered the rear, broke more than five hundred Liang horsemen, and returned at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，莊宗與梁軍大戰於胡柳陂，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhuangzong fought a great battle with the Liang army at Huliu Slope; the forces were said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhuangzong fought a major battle with the Liang army at Huliu Slope, with forces on both sides said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 總管周德威將左軍，雜以燕人，前鋒不利，德威死之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Zhou Dewei led the left wing, mixed with Yan men; the vanguard fared poorly, and Dewei died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhou Dewei led the left wing with Yan troops mixed in. The vanguard fared badly, and Dewei was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 莊宗率步眾五千，固守高陵以避敵之銳。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong led five thousand infantry and held fast at Gaoling to avoid the enemy's sharp thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong led five thousand foot soldiers and held Gaoling to avoid the enemy's sharpest thrust.

sentences.zh: 明宗獨完右廣，伏於土山之下，顧謂帝曰：「梁人首獲其利，旌旗甚整，何計可以挫之？

translations.literal: Mingzong alone kept the right wing intact, concealed beneath an earthen hill, turned to the Emperor and said, "The Liang men have gained the first advantage; their banners are very orderly—what plan can break them?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong alone kept the right wing intact and lay concealed below an earthen hill. He turned to the emperor and said, "The Liang have taken the first advantage, and their banners stand in perfect order. What plan can break them?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「臘後寒如此，出手墮指，彼多步眾，易進難退，莫若啜糒飲水，徐而困之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "After the twelfth month the cold is such that fingers fall off when one puts out a hand; they have mostly infantry, easy to advance but hard to retreat—better to sip dry rations and drink water and wear them down slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "After the twelfth month the cold is so fierce that fingers freeze when you reach out. They are mostly infantry—easy to advance but hard to retreat. Better to let them gnaw dry rations and drink water while we wear them down slowly."

sentences.zh: 且超乘徒行，其勢不等，一擊而破，期在必勝。

translations.literal: Moreover, cavalry against foot soldiers—their momentum is unequal; one strike will break them, and victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, horsemen against foot soldiers—their momentum cannot be equal. One strike will break them, and victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「是吾心也。

translations.literal: Mingzong said, "That is exactly my thought."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "That is exactly what I had in mind."

sentences.zh: 」會日暮，梁軍列於平野，五六萬人為一方陣，麾遊騎以迫唐軍，帝曰：「敵將遁矣！

translations.literal: As evening fell, the Liang army drew up on the open plain, fifty or sixty thousand men in a single square formation, and directed their light cavalry to press the Tang army; the Emperor said, "The enemy is about to flee!"
translations.idiomatic: As evening fell, the Liang army formed on the open plain in a single square of fifty or sixty thousand men and sent their light cavalry to press the Tang forces. The emperor said, "The enemy is about to flee!"

sentences.zh: 」乃請明宗令士整胄，寬而羅之，命左射軍三百人鳴矢馳轉，漸束其勢，以數千騎合之。

translations.literal: He then asked Mingzong to order the soldiers to don their armor, spread out wide and encircle them, commanded three hundred left-hand archers to shoot whistling arrows while wheeling about, gradually tightening their momentum, and joined them with several thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Mingzong to have the men arm themselves, spread out wide to encircle the enemy, and sent three hundred left-hand archers to wheel about shooting whistling arrows, gradually tightening the ring until several thousand horsemen closed in together.

sentences.zh: 迨夜，旌旗皆靡，而一角先潰，三面踵之，其牙竿相擊，若火爆之聲，橫屍積甲，不可勝計。

translations.literal: By night the banners all drooped; one corner collapsed first, and the other three sides followed; their command pennants struck one another with a sound like exploding fire; corpses and armor lay heaped beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: By night their banners had all gone slack. One corner of the formation broke first, and the other three sides collapsed in its wake. Their command pennants clashed with a sound like exploding fire, and corpses and armor lay heaped beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 由是梁人勢削，莊宗進營德勝渡。

translations.literal: From this the Liang forces' strength was reduced, and Zhuangzong advanced his camp to Desheng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Liang forces were greatly weakened, and Zhuangzong advanced his camp to Desheng Ford.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月，又從明宗戰梁人於德勝渡，敗其將戴思遠，殺二萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year he again followed Mingzong in fighting the Liang at Desheng Ford, defeated their general Dai Siyuan, and killed more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year he again fought the Liang at Desheng Ford at Mingzong's side, defeated their general Dai Siyuan, and killed more than twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十九年，戰胡盧套，唐軍稍卻，帝睹其敵銳，拔劍辟道，肩護明宗而退，敵人望之，無敢襲者。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year they fought at Hulu Tao; the Tang army fell back slightly; the Emperor saw the enemy's sharp thrust, drew his sword to clear a path, shielded Mingzong with his shoulder as they withdrew, and the enemy, seeing this, dared not press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year they fought at Hulu Tao. The Tang army gave ground slightly, but when the emperor saw the enemy pressing hard he drew his sword to clear a path and shielded Mingzong with his shoulder as they withdrew. The enemy, seeing him, dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 二十年十月，從明宗觀梁人之楊村寨，部曲皆不擐甲，俄而敵出不意，以兵掩明宗，刃將及背，帝挾戰戟而進，一擊而兇酋落馬者數輩，明宗遂解其難。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he followed Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangjia Stockade; the troops were all without armor; suddenly the enemy came out unexpectedly and surrounded Mingzong with troops; blades were about to reach his back; the Emperor charged forward gripping his battle halberd, and with one strike several fierce chieftains fell from their horses; Mingzong was thus delivered from danger.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he accompanied Mingzong to observe the Liang at Yangjia Stockade. The troops had not put on their armor when the enemy suddenly appeared and surrounded Mingzong. Blades were about to reach his back when the emperor charged forward with his battle halberd and, with a single blow, knocked several enemy chieftains from their horses. Mingzong was thus delivered from danger.

sentences.zh: 是歲，莊宗即位於鄴，改元同光，遣明宗越河，懸軍深入以取鄆。

translations.literal: That year Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye, changed the era name to Tongguang, and dispatched Mingzong across the river with a detached force to drive deep and capture Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye and changed the era name to Tongguang. He sent Mingzong across the river with a detached force to drive deep inland and capture Yan.

sentences.zh: 鄆人始不之覺，帝以五十騎從明宗涉濟，突東門而入。

translations.literal: The men of Yan at first did not perceive them; the Emperor with fifty horsemen followed Mingzong across the ford and burst in through the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders of Yan at first did not notice them. The emperor followed Mingzong across the ford with fifty horsemen and burst in through the east gate.

sentences.zh: 鄆兵來拒，帝中刃，翼明宗，羅兵通衢，嶷然不動。

translations.literal: Yan troops came to resist; the Emperor was struck by a blade; he shielded Mingzong, arrayed troops across the thoroughfare, and stood firm without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Yan troops came out to resist. The emperor was struck by a blade, but he shielded Mingzong, drew up his men across the main thoroughfare, and stood firm without yielding.

sentences.zh: 會後騎繼至，遂拔中城以據之。

translations.literal: When the rear cavalry arrived in succession, they then stormed the inner city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rear cavalry came up, they stormed the inner city and held it.

sentences.zh: 既而平汴水，滅梁室，成莊宗一統，集明宗大勛，帝與唐末帝功居最，莊宗朝官未顯者，以帝不好矜伐故也，唯明宗心知之。

translations.literal: Thereafter they pacified the Bian River region, destroyed the Liang house, completed Zhuangzong's unification, and gathered Mingzong's great merit; the Emperor and the Last Emperor of Tang ranked highest in achievement; at Zhuangzong's court he was not yet prominent, because the Emperor did not like boasting of his deeds—only Mingzong knew this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they pacified the Bian River region, destroyed the Liang dynasty, and completed Zhuangzong's unification, while Mingzong gathered the greatest share of merit. The emperor and the Last Emperor of Tang stood foremost in achievement, yet at Zhuangzong's court he remained little noticed because he did not care to boast of his deeds. Only Mingzong understood this in his heart.

sentences.zh: 同光四年二月，趙在禮據鄴為亂，朝廷遣元行欽招之不下，群議紛然，以為非明宗不可，莊宗乃以明宗為統帥。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili seized Ye in rebellion; the court sent Yuan Xingqin to summon him but he would not submit; opinion was divided, and it was held that only Mingzong could handle it; Zhuangzong then appointed Mingzong commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili seized Ye in rebellion. The court sent Yuan Xingqin to win him over, but he would not submit. Opinion in court was divided, and many held that only Mingzong could resolve the crisis. Zhuangzong then appointed Mingzong commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時帝從行，至魏，諸軍有變，叩馬請明宗帝河北。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor accompanied the campaign; when they reached Wei, the armies mutinied, seized Mingzong's horse, and begged him to declare himself emperor in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accompanied the campaign. When they reached Wei the armies mutinied, seized Mingzong's horse, and begged him to declare himself emperor in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 明宗受霍彥威勸，將自訴於天子，遂佯諾。

translations.literal: Mingzong, persuaded by Huo Yanwei, intended to plead his case before the Son of Heaven, and therefore pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Persuaded by Huo Yanwei, Mingzong intended to plead his innocence before the Son of Heaven and therefore pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 諸軍亦恐事不果，而散者甚眾，明宗所全者，唯常山一軍而已。

translations.literal: The armies also feared the affair would not succeed, and very many dispersed; all Mingzong retained was the Changshan army alone.
translations.idiomatic: The troops also feared the affair would fail, and a great many dispersed. All Mingzong retained was the Changshan army alone.

sentences.zh: 西次魏縣，帝密言於明宗曰：「猶豫者兵家大忌，必若求訴，宜決其行。

translations.literal: They halted west at Weixian; the Emperor spoke privately to Mingzong and said, "Hesitation is the great taboo of military affairs; if you truly wish to plead your case, you should decide your course at once."
translations.idiomatic: They halted west at Weixian. The emperor spoke privately to Mingzong and said, "Hesitation is the great taboo in warfare. If you truly mean to plead your case, you must decide your course at once."

sentences.zh: 某願率三百騎先趨汴水，以探虎口，如遂其志，請大軍速進。

translations.literal: I am willing to lead three hundred horsemen ahead to the Bian River to probe the tiger's maw; if your purpose is fulfilled, I ask that the main army advance swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to lead three hundred horsemen ahead to the Bian River to probe the danger. If your purpose succeeds, let the main army advance at once."

sentences.zh: 夷門者，天下之要害也，據之可以自雪。

translations.literal: Yimen is the vital point of the realm; holding it, one can clear oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Yimen is the vital point of the realm. Hold it, and you can clear your own name.

sentences.zh: 安有上將與三軍言變，他日有平手乎！

translations.literal: How can a supreme commander speak of mutiny with the whole army—will there ever be a draw afterward!
translations.idiomatic: How can a supreme commander discuss mutiny with the whole army and expect anything but ruin afterward!

sentences.zh: 危在頃刻，不宜恬然。

translations.literal: Danger is in the next moment; one should not remain at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Danger is upon us in the next moment. You must not remain at ease.

sentences.zh: 」明宗至相州，遂分驍騎三百付之，遣帝由黎陽濟河，自汴西門而入，因據其城。

translations.literal: Mingzong reached Xiangzhou, then divided out three hundred elite horsemen and gave them to him, dispatching the Emperor to cross the river at Liyang, enter through Bian's west gate, and thereby seize the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong reached Xiangzhou, detached three hundred elite horsemen for him, and sent the emperor to cross the river at Liyang, enter through Bian's west gate, and seize the city.

sentences.zh: 及明宗入汴，莊宗親統師亦至城之西北五里，登高嘆曰：「吾不濟矣！

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Bian, Zhuangzong personally commanding his army also reached a point five li northwest of the city; he climbed high and sighed, "I shall not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Bian, Zhuangzong, leading his army in person, also reached a point five li northwest of the city. He climbed to a height and sighed, "I am finished!"

sentences.zh: 」由此莊宗從兵大潰，來歸明宗。

translations.literal: From this Zhuangzong's following troops collapsed in great disorder and came over to Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: From this Zhuangzong's following troops collapsed in great disorder and came over to Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗尋遣帝令率兵為前鋒，趨汜水關。

translations.literal: Mingzong soon dispatched the Emperor to lead troops as vanguard and hurry to Sishui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong soon sent the emperor ahead as vanguard to hurry toward Sishui Pass.

sentences.zh: 俄而莊宗遇內難而崩。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zhuangzong met internal turmoil and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhuangzong was caught in internal turmoil and died.

sentences.zh: 是月，明宗入洛，嘉帝之功，自總管府都校署陜府兵馬留後。

translations.literal: That month Mingzong entered Luoyang, commended the Emperor's achievements, and promoted him from commander of the commandery staff to military commissioner of Shaanfu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Mingzong entered Luoyang, praised the emperor's achievements, and promoted him from commander of the commandery staff to military commissioner of Shaanfu.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，改元天成，五月，加帝光祿大夫、檢校司徒，充陜州保義軍節度使，歲未期而軍民之政大治焉。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he changed the era name to Tiancheng; in the fifth month he advanced the Emperor to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Minister of Works, and appointed him military governor of the Baoyi Army of Shaanzhou; before a year had passed both military and civil administration were greatly well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he changed the era name to Tiancheng. In the fifth month he advanced the emperor to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Minister of Works and appointed him military governor of the Baoyi Army at Shaanzhou. Before a year had passed both military and civil affairs were in excellent order.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，加檢校太傅兼六軍諸衛副使，進封開國伯，增食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year he was advanced to Honorary Grand Mentor and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards, enfeoffed as Baron of the State-Founding line, and given an additional four hundred households in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year he was advanced to Honorary Grand Mentor and made Deputy Commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards. He was enfeoffed as Baron of the State-Founding line and given an additional four hundred households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝赴闕，以倅六軍諸衛事故也。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor went to court on account of his duties as deputy commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor went to court in connection with his duties as deputy commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 八月，加食邑八百戶，實封一百戶，旌為政之效也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month his fief was increased by eight hundred households and his actual enfeoffment by one hundred households, in recognition of the effects of his governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his fief was increased by eight hundred households and his actual enfeoffment by one hundred, in recognition of the success of his governance.

sentences.zh: 十月，明宗幸汴，以帝為御營使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Mingzong visited Bian and appointed the Emperor Imperial Camp Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Mingzong visited Bian and appointed the emperor Imperial Camp Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 車駕次京水，飛報汴州節度使朱守殷叛，明宗命帝董親軍倍道星行，信宿及浚城，一戰而拔之。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Jingshui; urgent reports arrived that Bianzhou military governor Zhu Shouyin had rebelled; Mingzong ordered the Emperor to lead the personal army by forced marches day and night; within two nights he reached Jun City and took it in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage halted at Jingshui when urgent reports arrived that Zhu Shouyin, military governor of Bianzhou, had rebelled. Mingzong ordered the emperor to lead the personal army by forced marches day and night. Within two nights he reached Jun City and took it in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 尋以帝為宣武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使兼六軍諸衛副使，進封開國公，加食邑五百戶，賜耀忠匡定保節功臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Emperor was made military governor of the Xuanwu Army, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry, and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards; he was advanced to Duke of the State-Founding line, given an additional five hundred households in his fief, and granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectifying Settlement, and Preserving Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed military governor of the Xuanwu Army, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry, and Deputy Commissioner of the Six Armies and Palace Guards. He was advanced to Duke of the State-Founding line, given an additional five hundred households in his fief, and granted the title Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectifying Settlement, and Preserving Integrity.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，車駕還洛，制加檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事、興唐尹、鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang; by edict he was advanced to Honorary Grand Mentor, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Prefect of Xingtang, Garrison Commander of Ye Capital, and Military Governor of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang. By edict he was advanced to Honorary Grand Mentor, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Prefect of Xingtang, Garrison Commander of Ye Capital, and Military Governor of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he was advanced to Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he was advanced to Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦王從榮奏：「伏見北面頻奏報，契丹族移帳近塞，吐渾、突厥已侵邊地，戍兵雖多，未有統帥，早宜命大將一人，以安雲、朔。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qin Congrong memorialized, "I observe that the northern frontier has repeatedly reported that the Khitan tribes have moved their camps close to the border, and the Tuyuhun and Turks have already invaded the frontier; though garrison troops are numerous, there is as yet no commander-in-chief; a great general should early be appointed to secure Yun and Shuo."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Congrong of Qin memorialized, "Reports from the northern frontier say repeatedly that the Khitan have moved their camps close to the border, and that the Tuyuhun and Turks have already invaded our territory. Though the garrisons are numerous, they have no commander. A great general should be appointed at once to secure Yun and Shuo."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「卿等商量。

translations.literal: Mingzong said, "You ministers should deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "You ministers should deliberate among yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」從榮與諸大臣奏曰：「將校之中，唯石敬瑭、康義誠二人可行。

translations.literal: Congrong and the various ministers memorialized, "Among the commanders, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng are fit for the task."
translations.idiomatic: Congrong and the ministers memorialized together, "Among the commanders, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng are fit for the task."

sentences.zh: 」帝素不欲為禁軍之副，即奏曰：「臣願北行。

translations.literal: The Emperor had never wished to serve as deputy of the Palace Guard; he immediately memorialized, "Your subject is willing to go north."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never wished to serve as deputy of the Palace Guard. He immediately memorialized, "Your subject is willing to go north."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「卿為吾行，事無不濟。

translations.literal: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, nothing will fail to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, nothing will fail to succeed."

sentences.zh: 」及受詔，不落六軍副使，帝復遷延辭避。

translations.literal: When he received the edict without being removed from the post of deputy commissioner of the Six Armies, the Emperor again delayed and declined.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the edict without being relieved of his post as deputy commissioner of the Six Armies, the emperor again delayed and declined.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙酉，明宗復謂侍臣曰：「雲州奏，契丹自幽州移帳，言就放牧，終冬不退，其患深矣。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month Mingzong again said to his attending ministers, "Yunzhou reports that the Khitan have moved their camps from Youzhou, claiming they are coming to pasture, yet they have not withdrawn through the whole winter—the peril is grave."
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month Mingzong again told his attending ministers, "Yunzhou reports that the Khitan have moved their camps from Youzhou, claiming they have come to pasture, yet they have not withdrawn through the whole winter. The peril is grave."

sentences.zh: 」樞密使範延光奏曰：「已議石敬瑭與康義誠北行，然其定奪，即在宸旨。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Fan Yanguang memorialized, "Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng have already been discussed for the northern campaign, but the final decision rests with Your Majesty's sacred will."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Fan Yanguang memorialized, "Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng have already been discussed for the northern campaign, but the final decision rests with Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝奏曰：「臣雖不才，爭敢避事，但進退惟命。

translations.literal: The Emperor memorialized, "Though your subject lacks talent, how would he dare avoid duty? Only advance or retreat awaits Your Majesty's command."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor memorialized, "Though your subject lacks talent, how could he dare avoid duty? Only advance or retreat await Your Majesty's command."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「卿為吾行，甚葉眾議。

translations.literal: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, that accords very well with public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, that accords very well with what everyone expects."

sentences.zh: 」由是遂定。

translations.literal: From this the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: From this the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，加兼侍中、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，兼大同、振武、彰國、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步軍總管，改賜竭忠匡運寧國功臣。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day he was advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant, Prefect of Taiyuan, Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital, Military Governor of Hedong, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese and tribal cavalry and infantry of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies; his title was changed to Meritorious Minister for Exhausting Loyalty, Rectifying Transport, and Pacifying the State.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day he was advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant, Prefect of Taiyuan, Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital, and Military Governor of Hedong, and made Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese and tribal cavalry and infantry of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies. His title was changed to Meritorious Minister for Exhausting Loyalty, Rectifying Transport, and Pacifying the State.

sentences.zh: 翌日，宴於中興殿，帝捧觴上壽，因奏曰：「臣雖微怯，惟邊事敢不盡其忠力，但臣遠違玉階，無以時申補報。

translations.literal: The next day a banquet was held in the Zhongxing Hall; the Emperor raised his cup to offer longevity and then memorialized, "Though your subject is slight and timid, in frontier affairs he dares not fail to exhaust loyalty and strength; yet your subject will be far from the jade steps and unable to offer timely recompense."
translations.idiomatic: The next day a banquet was held in the Zhongxing Hall. The emperor raised his cup to offer longevity and then said, "Though your subject is slight and timid, in frontier affairs he dares not fail to give his full loyalty and strength. Yet I shall be far from the jade steps and unable to repay Your Majesty in timely fashion."

sentences.zh: 」帝因再拜告辭，明宗泣下沾衿。

translations.literal: The Emperor then bowed twice to take leave; Mingzong's tears fell and soaked his collar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice to take his leave, and Mingzong's tears fell and soaked his collar.

sentences.zh: 左右怪其過傷，果與帝因此為訣，不復相見矣。

translations.literal: Those at his side wondered at his excessive grief; indeed, from this the Emperor took his farewell, and they never met again.
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side wondered at his excessive grief. Indeed, from this parting the emperor and Mingzong never met again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，明宗晏駕，帝聞之，長慟若喪考妣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Mingzong died; when the Emperor heard of it, he mourned long as though he had lost father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mingzong died. When the emperor heard the news, he mourned at length as though he had lost his own father and mother.

sentences.zh: 應順元年正月，閔帝即位，加中書令，及增食邑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Emperor Min took the throne; the Emperor was advanced to Director of the Secretariat and given an increase in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Emperor Min took the throne. The emperor was advanced to Director of the Secretariat and given an increase in his fief.

sentences.zh: 帝性簡儉，未嘗以聲色滋味輒自宴樂，每公退，必召幕客論民間利害及刑政得失，明而難犯，事多親決。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was simple and frugal; he never indulged himself in music, women, or fine flavors for his own pleasure; whenever official business ended, he always summoned his staff to discuss the people's gains and losses and the successes and failures of penal administration; he was clear-minded and hard to offend, and many matters he decided in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was simple and frugal by nature. He never indulged himself in music, women, or fine food for his own pleasure. Whenever official business ended, he summoned his staff to discuss the people's welfare and the successes and failures of penal administration. He was clear-minded and not easily crossed, and he decided many matters in person.

sentences.zh: 有店婦與軍士訟，云「曝粟於門，為馬所食」。

translations.literal: A shopkeeper's wife disputed with a soldier, saying, "I spread grain to dry at the door, and it was eaten by a horse."
translations.idiomatic: A shopkeeper's wife brought suit against a soldier, claiming, "I spread grain to dry at my door, and a horse ate it."

sentences.zh: 而軍士懇訴，無以自明。

translations.literal: The soldier pleaded earnestly but had no way to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier pleaded earnestly but had no way to prove his innocence.

sentences.zh: 帝謂鞫吏曰：「兩訟未分，何以為斷？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the examining clerk, "The two suits are not yet divided—how can there be a judgment?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the examining clerk, "The two sides have not yet been distinguished. How can there be a judgment?"

sentences.zh: 可殺馬刳腸而視其粟，有則軍士誅，無則婦人死。

translations.literal: Kill the horse, cut open its belly, and look for grain; if there is grain, execute the soldier; if not, the woman dies."
translations.idiomatic: Kill the horse, cut open its belly, and look for grain. If there is grain, execute the soldier; if not, the woman dies."

sentences.zh: 」遂殺馬，馬腸無粟，因戮其婦人。

translations.literal: They then killed the horse; there was no grain in its belly, and therefore the woman was executed.
translations.idiomatic: They killed the horse. There was no grain in its belly, and the woman was executed.

sentences.zh: 境內肅然，莫敢以欺事言者。

translations.literal: Within the territory all were solemn; none dared speak of deceitful affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within his territory all were solemn, and none dared bring a deceitful suit.

sentences.zh: 三月，移鎮常山。

translations.literal: In the third month he was transferred to garrison Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was transferred to garrison Changshan.

sentences.zh: 所歷方鎮，以孝治為急，見民間父母在昆弟分索者，必繩而殺之。

translations.literal: In every circuit he governed, he made filial governance urgent; whenever he saw among the people parents and children divided in property disputes among brothers, he always bound and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In every circuit he governed he made filial conduct the first priority. Whenever he found parents and children entangled in property disputes among brothers, he had them bound and executed.

sentences.zh: 勤於吏事，廷無滯訟。

translations.literal: He was diligent in official business, and in court there were no delayed lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in official business, and no lawsuit lingered in his court.

sentences.zh: 常山屬邑曰九門，有人鬻地與異居兄，議價不定，乃移於他人。

translations.literal: A subordinate county of Changshan called Jiumen had a man who sold land to a brother living separately; the price was not settled, and he therefore transferred the sale to another person.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiumen, a subordinate county of Changshan, a man tried to sell land to a brother living separately. When they could not agree on a price, he offered the land to someone else.

sentences.zh: 他人須兄立券，兄固抑之，因訴於令。

translations.literal: The other person required the brother to draw up a contract; the brother firmly refused, and therefore the matter was brought before the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The other buyer required the brother to draw up a contract, but the brother firmly refused, and the matter was brought before the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 令以弟兄俱不義，送府。

translations.literal: The magistrate held that both brothers were unrighteous and sent the case to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate held that both brothers were in the wrong and sent the case to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 帝監之曰：「人之不義，由牧長新至，教化所未能及，吾甚愧焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor reviewed the case and said, "Men's lack of righteousness comes from the pastoral chief having newly arrived and instruction not yet reaching them—I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the case and said, "When men behave without righteousness, it is because their governor has only lately arrived and instruction has not yet reached them. I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 若以至理言之，兄利良田，弟求善價，順之則是，沮之則非，其兄不義之甚也，宜重笞焉。

translations.literal: If one speaks by ultimate principle, the elder brother coveted fertile fields and the younger sought a fair price; to comply would be right, to obstruct would be wrong—the elder brother was deeply unrighteous and should receive heavy beating.
translations.idiomatic: By ultimate right, the elder brother coveted fertile land while the younger sought a fair price. To comply would be right and to obstruct wrong. The elder brother was deeply in the wrong and deserved a heavy beating.

sentences.zh: 市田以高價者取之。

translations.literal: The field was sold to whoever offered the higher price.
translations.idiomatic: The field was sold to whoever offered the higher price.

sentences.zh: 」上下服其明。

translations.literal: Above and below were convinced by his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were convinced by his clarity of judgment.

sentences.zh: 及岐陽兵亂，推潞王為天子，閔帝急詔帝赴闕，欲以社稷為托。

translations.literal: When the Qiyang troops rebelled and installed the Prince of Lu as Son of Heaven, Emperor Min urgently summoned the Emperor to court, intending to entrust the altars of state to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiyang troops rebelled and installed the Prince of Lu as emperor, Emperor Min urgently summoned him to court, intending to entrust the realm to him.

sentences.zh: 閔帝自洛陽出奔於衛，相遇於途，遂與閔帝回入衛州。

translations.literal: Emperor Min fled from Luoyang toward Wei; they met on the road, and the Emperor then returned with Emperor Min into Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min fled Luoyang toward Wei. They met on the road, and the emperor returned with him into Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時閔帝左右將不利於帝，帝覺之，因擒其從騎百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time those at Emperor Min's side intended harm to the Emperor; he perceived this and therefore seized more than a hundred of their attendant horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those around Emperor Min intended harm against him. He perceived it and seized more than a hundred of their attendant horsemen.

sentences.zh: 閔帝知事不濟，與帝長慟而別，帝遣刺史王宏贄安置閔帝於公舍而去，尋為潞王所害，帝後長以此愧心焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Min knew the affair would not succeed and parted from the Emperor after long lamentation; the Emperor sent Prefect Wang Hongzan to lodge Emperor Min in the public residence and then departed; soon afterward Emperor Min was killed by the Prince of Lu; the Emperor long afterward felt shame in his heart over this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min knew the affair was lost and parted from him after long lamentation. The emperor sent Prefect Wang Hongzan to lodge Emperor Min in the public residence and then departed. Soon afterward Emperor Min was killed by the Prince of Lu, and the emperor long carried this as a burden on his conscience.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年五月，復授太原節度使、北京留守，充大同、振武、彰國、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai he was again appointed Military Governor of Taiyuan, Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital, and Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese and tribal cavalry and infantry of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai he was again appointed military governor of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and commander-in-chief of the Chinese and tribal cavalry and infantry of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，帝屯軍於忻州，朝廷遣使送夏衣，傳詔撫諭，後軍人遽呼萬歲者數四，帝懼，斬挾馬將李暉以下三十餘人以徇，乃止。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year the Emperor encamped his army at Xinzhou; the court sent envoys bearing summer garments and an edict of reassurance; afterward soldiers suddenly shouted "Long live!" four times; the Emperor was afraid, executed the horse-gripping general Li Hui and more than thirty others below him as a warning, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year he encamped at Xinzhou. The court sent envoys with summer garments and a reassuring edict, but afterward the soldiers suddenly shouted "Long live the emperor!" four times. Alarmed, he executed the horse-gripping general Li Hui and more than thirty others as a warning, and only then did it stop.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，移授鄆州節度使，進封趙國公，仍改扶天啟運中正功臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to Military Governor of Yanzhou, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and his title was changed to Meritorious Minister for Upholding Heaven, Initiating Fortune, and Central Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to military governor of Yanzhou, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and given the title Meritorious Minister for Upholding Heaven, Initiating Fortune, and Central Rectitude.

sentences.zh: 尋降詔促帝赴任。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued urging the Emperor to proceed to his new post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict was issued ordering him to proceed to his new post at once.

sentences.zh: 帝心疑之，乃召僚佐議曰：「孤再受太原之日，主上面宣云：『與卿北門，一生無議除改。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew suspicious in his heart and therefore summoned his staff to deliberate, saying, "When I again received Taiyuan, the sovereign announced to my face, 'I give you the northern gate; in your lifetime there shall be no discussion of removal or transfer.'"
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious, he summoned his staff and said, "When I was again given Taiyuan, the sovereign announced to my face, 'I give you the northern gate; in your lifetime there shall be no talk of removing or transferring you.'"

sentences.zh: 』今忽降此命，莫是以去年忻州亂兵見迫，過相猜乎？

translations.literal: Now this command has suddenly come down—is it because last year at Xinzhou the mutinous troops pressed upon me, and there is excessive mutual suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: Now this command has suddenly come down. Is it because last year at Xinzhou the mutinous troops pressed upon me, and suspicion has grown too great?"

sentences.zh: 又今年千春節，公主入覲，當辭時，謂公主曰：『爾歸心甚急，欲與石郎反耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, at this year's Thousand Springs Festival, when the princess came to court and was taking leave, he said to the princess, 'Your heart to return is very urgent—do you wish to rebel with Master Shi?'"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at this year's Thousand Springs Festival, when the princess came to court and was taking leave, the sovereign said to her, 'Your heart to return is very urgent—do you mean to rebel with Master Shi?'"

sentences.zh: 』此疑我之狀固且明矣。

translations.literal: This suspicion of me is already quite clear.
translations.idiomatic: His suspicion of me is already perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 今天子用後族，委邪臣，沈湎荒惑，萬機停壅，失刑失賞，不亡何待！

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven employs the empress's kin, entrusts affairs to wicked ministers, sinks in dissipation and delusion, and all government stalls and clogs; punishments and rewards are lost—if he does not perish, what is he waiting for!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven now employs the empress's kin, entrusts power to wicked ministers, and sinks in dissipation and delusion until all government stalls. Punishments and rewards are lost. If such a ruler does not perish, what is he waiting for!

sentences.zh: 吾自應順中少主出奔之日，睹人情大去，不能扶危持顛，憤憤於方寸者三年矣。

translations.literal: From the day in Yingshun when the young sovereign fled, I have seen popular sentiment largely depart and have been unable to shore up peril and uphold collapse; indignation has burned in my breast for three years.
translations.idiomatic: From the day in Yingshun when the young sovereign fled, I have seen the people's hearts depart and have been unable to shore up a failing state. Indignation has burned in my breast for three years.

sentences.zh: 今我無異志，朝廷自啟禍機，不可安然死於道路。

translations.literal: Now I have no rebellious intent, but the court itself has opened the door to calamity; I cannot calmly die on the road.
translations.idiomatic: I have no rebellious intent, but the court itself has opened the door to calamity. I cannot calmly die on the road.

sentences.zh: 況太原險固之地，積粟甚多，若且寬我，我當奉之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Taiyuan is a perilous and secure place with grain stored in great abundance; if they will only spare me for a time, I shall serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Taiyuan is a strong and secure place with abundant grain stores. If they will only spare me for a time, I shall remain loyal.

sentences.zh: 必若加兵，我則外告鄰方，北構強敵，興亡之數，皎皎在天。

translations.literal: If they must send troops against me, I shall appeal to neighboring states abroad and ally with powerful enemies to the north; the number of rise and fall shines bright in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If they send troops against me, I shall appeal to neighboring states and ally with powerful enemies to the north. The fate of rise and fall shines bright in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今欲發表稱疾，以俟其意，諸公以為何如？」

translations.literal: Now I wish to send a memorial claiming illness to await their intent—what do you gentlemen think of this?"
translations.idiomatic: I now wish to send a memorial claiming illness to await their intent. What do you gentlemen think of this?"

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：晉祖在並部，嘗從容謂賓佐云：「近因晝寢，忽夢若頃年在洛京時，與天子連鑣於路，過舊第，天子請某入其第，某遜讓者數四，不得已即促轡而入，至廳事下馬，升自阼階，西向而坐，天子已馳車去矣。

translations.literal: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: The Ancestor of Jin, while in Bingbu, once said calmly to his guests and staff, "Recently during a daytime nap I suddenly dreamed that, as in years past at Luoyang, I was riding side by side with the Son of Heaven on the road. We passed my old residence, and the Son of Heaven asked me to enter it. I declined several times, but unable to refuse further I urged my horse in. Reaching the main hall I dismounted, ascended from the eastern steps, and sat facing west, while the Son of Heaven had already driven his carriage away."
translations.idiomatic: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall: While in Bing, the founder of Jin once said calmly to his staff, "Recently during a daytime nap I dreamed that, as in years past at Luoyang, I was riding side by side with the Son of Heaven. We passed my old residence, and the Son of Heaven asked me to enter it. I declined several times, but at last I urged my horse in. In the main hall I dismounted, ascended from the eastern steps, and sat facing west, while the Son of Heaven had already driven away."

sentences.zh: 其夢如此。

translations.literal: The dream was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the dream.

sentences.zh: 」群僚莫敢有所答。

translations.literal: The assembled officials dared make no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled officials dared make no reply.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，果有鼎革之事。

translations.literal: That winter there was indeed a change of the dynastic cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was indeed a change of dynasty.

sentences.zh: 蓋晉祖懷不軌之心久矣，故托夢以惑眾也。）〉

translations.literal: The Ancestor of Jin had long harbored rebellious intent and therefore used a dream to mislead the multitude.)
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Jin had long harbored rebellious intent and therefore used a dream to mislead those around him.)

sentences.zh: 掌書記桑維翰、都押衙劉知遠贊成密計，遂拒末帝之命。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Sang Weihan and Chief Escort Officer Liu Zhiyuan approved the secret plan, and he therefore refused the Last Emperor's command.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Sang Weihan and Chief Escort Officer Liu Zhiyuan approved the secret plan, and he therefore refused the Last Emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以帝不奉詔，降旨削奪官爵，即詔晉州刺史、北面副招討使張敬達領兵圍帝於晉陽。

translations.literal: Because the Emperor did not obey the edict, the court issued an order stripping his offices and titles, and immediately commanded Jinzhou Prefect and Northern Deputy Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jingda to lead troops and besiege the Emperor at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because he did not obey the edict, the court stripped his offices and titles and immediately ordered Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Jingda, deputy northern pacification commissioner, to lead troops and besiege him at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝尋命桑維翰詣諸道求援，契丹遣人復書諾之，約以中秋赴義。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon ordered Sang Weihan to go to the various circuits seeking aid; the Khitan sent men with a reply promising assistance, agreeing to come to his aid by the Mid-Autumn Festival.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent Sang Weihan to the various circuits seeking aid. The Khitan replied with a promise of assistance, agreeing to come by the Mid-Autumn Festival.

sentences.zh: （《遼史太宗紀》云：七月丙申，唐河東節度使石敬瑭為其主所討，遣趙瑩求救，時趙德鈞亦遣使至，河東復遣桑維翰來告急，遂許興師。

translations.literal: (The Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong in the History of Liao states: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, Tang's Hedong Military Governor Shi Jingtang, being attacked by his sovereign, sent Zhao Ying to seek rescue; at that time Zhao Dejun also sent envoys; Hedong again sent Sang Weihan to report urgency, and troops were then promised.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Taizong Annals in the History of Liao states: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, Tang's Hedong military governor Shi Jingtang, attacked by his sovereign, sent Zhao Ying to seek rescue. Zhao Dejun also sent envoys, and Hedong again sent Sang Weihan in urgent appeal, whereupon troops were promised.)

sentences.zh: 八月庚午，自將以援敬瑭。）〉

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the eighth month he personally led troops to aid Jingtang.)
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eighth month he personally led troops to aid Jingtang.)

sentences.zh: 六月，北面招收指揮使安重榮以部曲數千人入城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Northern Recruitment and Acceptance Commissioner An Chongrong entered the city with several thousand men of his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the northern recruitment commissioner An Chongrong entered the city with several thousand men of his personal following.

sentences.zh: 七月，代州屯將安元信率一軍，與西北面先鋒指揮使安審信引五百騎俱至。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the garrison commander of Daizhou, An Yuanxin, led one army, and together with the Northwestern Vanguard Commander An Shenxin brought five hundred horsemen, all arriving.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Daizhou garrison commander An Yuanxin led one army, and together with the northwestern vanguard commander An Shenxin brought five hundred horsemen to join him.

sentences.zh: 八月，懷州彰聖軍使張萬迪等各率千餘騎來降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhang Wandi, commissioner of the Zhangsheng Army of Huaizhou, and others each led more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhang Wandi, commander of the Zhangsheng Army at Huaizhou, and others each led more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.

sentences.zh: 是月，外眾攻我甚急，帝親當矢石，人心雖固，廩食漸困。

translations.literal: That month the outer host pressed the attack very urgently; the Emperor personally faced arrows and stones; though hearts remained firm, granary provisions grew strained.
translations.idiomatic: That month the besieging army pressed the attack fiercely. The emperor personally faced arrows and stones. Though morale held firm, provisions in the granaries grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，契丹主率眾自雁門而南，旌騎不絕五十里餘。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the ninth month the Khitan ruler led his host south from Yanmen; banners and horsemen extended without break for more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the ninth month the Khitan ruler led his host south from Yanmen, banners and horsemen stretching without break for more than fifty li.

sentences.zh: （《遼史》：九月丁酉，入雁門。

translations.literal: (The History of Liao: On the dingyou day of the ninth month he entered Yanmen.)
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Liao: On the dingyou day of the ninth month he entered Yanmen.)

sentences.zh: 戊戌，次忻州。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day he halted at Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day he halted at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，次太原。）〉

translations.literal: On the jihai day he halted at Taiyuan.)
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day he halted at Taiyuan.)

sentences.zh: 先使人報帝云：「吾欲今日便破賊，可乎？

translations.literal: He first sent a man to report to the Emperor, "I wish to break the enemy today—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: He first sent word to the emperor, "I wish to break the enemy today. May I?"

sentences.zh: 」帝使人馳告曰：「皇帝赴難，比要成功，賊勢至厚，可明旦穩審議戰，未為晚也。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a man in haste to report, "The Emperor has come to relieve distress and must succeed; the enemy's strength is very great—it would be better to deliberate war calmly tomorrow morning, and that would not be late."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word in haste, "You have come to relieve distress and must succeed. The enemy is very strong. It would be better to deliberate calmly tomorrow morning; that would not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」使未達，契丹已與南軍騎將高行周、符彥卿等合戰。

translations.literal: Before the envoy arrived, the Khitan had already joined battle with the southern army's cavalry generals Gao Xingzhou, Fu Yanqing, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy arrived, the Khitan had already joined battle with the southern army's cavalry generals Gao Xingzhou, Fu Yanqing, and others.

sentences.zh: 時張敬達、楊光遠列陣西山下，士未及成伍，而行周、彥卿為伏兵所斷，舍軍而退，敬達等步兵大敗，死者萬人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan drew up ranks below the western hills; the soldiers had not yet formed ranks when Xingzhou and Yanqing were cut off by ambush troops, abandoned the army and withdrew, and Jingda's infantry suffered great defeat, with ten thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan had drawn up below the western hills, but before their men could form ranks, Xingzhou and Yanqing were cut off by ambush troops and withdrew. Jingda's infantry were routed, and ten thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 是夜，帝出北門與戎王相見，契丹主執帝手曰：「恨會面之晚。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor went out the north gate to meet the Rong king; the Khitan ruler took the Emperor's hand and said, "I regret that our meeting comes so late."
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor went out the north gate to meet the Khitan ruler, who took his hand and said, "I regret that our meeting comes so late."

sentences.zh: 」因論父子之義。

translations.literal: They then discussed the obligations of father and son.
translations.idiomatic: They then discussed the bond of father and son.

sentences.zh: （《遼史》：敬瑭率官屬來見，帝執手撫慰之。

translations.literal: (The History of Liao: Jingtang led his officials to come and see him; the Emperor took his hand and comforted him.)
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Liao: Jingtang led his officials to an audience; the Khitan emperor took his hand and comforted him.)

sentences.zh: 《契丹國志》云：敬瑭見契丹帝，問曰：「皇帝遠來，士馬疲倦，遽與唐大戰而勝，何也？

translations.literal: The Records of the Khitan State states: When Jingtang saw the Khitan Emperor, he asked, "The Emperor has come from afar; soldiers and horses are weary—how was it that you suddenly fought a great battle with Tang and won?"
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Khitan State states: When Jingtang met the Khitan emperor, he asked, "You have come from afar, and your men and horses are weary. How was it that you suddenly fought a great battle with Tang and won?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「始我謂唐必斷雁門諸路，伏兵險要，不可得進。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "At first I thought Tang would surely cut the roads through Yanmen and set ambush troops in perilous passes, so that advance would be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "At first I thought Tang would cut the roads through Yanmen and set ambush troops in the passes, so that we could not advance."

sentences.zh: 使人偵視皆無之，是以長驅而深入。

translations.literal: I sent men to reconnoiter and found none of this, and therefore drove far in a long advance.
translations.idiomatic: I sent scouts and found none of this, and therefore drove deep in a long advance.

sentences.zh: 我氣方銳，乘此擊之，是以勝之。

translations.literal: Our spirit was then at its keenest; seizing this moment we struck them, and therefore won.
translations.idiomatic: Our spirit was at its keenest. Seizing that moment we struck, and therefore won.

sentences.zh: 」敬瑭嘆服。）〉

translations.literal: Jingtang sighed in admiration.)
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang sighed in admiration.)

sentences.zh: 明日，帝與契丹圍敬達營寨，南軍不復出矣。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor and the Khitan besieged Jingda's camp; the southern army did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor and the Khitan besieged Jingda's camp, and the southern army did not come out again.

sentences.zh: 帝與契丹本無結好，自末帝見迫之後，遣心腹何福，以刀錯為信，一言親赴其難，迅若流電，信天意耶！

translations.literal: The Emperor and the Khitan originally had no alliance; after the Last Emperor pressed him, he sent his trusted man He Fu with a knife-file as token; with one word the Khitan ruler came in person to his distress, swift as flowing lightning—was this not Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the Khitan had had no prior alliance. After the Last Emperor pressed him, he sent his trusted man He Fu with a knife-file as token. At a single word the Khitan ruler came in person to his aid, swift as lightning. Was this not Heaven's intent!

sentences.zh: 己酉，唐末帝率親軍步騎三萬出次河橋。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day the Last Emperor of Tang led thirty thousand personal infantry and cavalry and went out to encamp at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day the Last Emperor of Tang led thirty thousand personal infantry and cavalry and encamped at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，末帝詔樞密使趙延壽分眾二萬為北面招討使，又詔魏博節度使範延光統本軍二萬人屯遼州。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day the Last Emperor decreed that Chief Councilor Zhao Yanshou divide twenty thousand men as Northern Pacification Commissioner, and also decreed that Weibo Military Governor Fan Yanguang command his own army of twenty thousand men to encamp at Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day the Last Emperor decreed that Chief Councilor Zhao Yanshou take twenty thousand men as northern pacification commissioner, and that Weibo military governor Fan Yanguang command twenty thousand men of his own army to encamp at Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，幽州節度使趙德鈞領所部萬餘人自上黨吳兒谷合延壽兵屯團柏谷，與敬達寨相去百里，彌月竟不能相通。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Youzhou Military Governor Zhao Dejun led more than ten thousand men of his command from Shangdang through Wu'er Valley to join Yanshou's troops and encamp at Tuanbai Valley; they were a hundred li from Jingda's stockade, yet for a full month they could not make contact.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Youzhou military governor Zhao Dejun led more than ten thousand of his men from Shangdang through Wu'er Valley to join Yanshou and encamp at Tuanbai Valley. They were a hundred li from Jingda's camp, yet for a full month they could not make contact.

sentences.zh: （《遼史》：初圍晉安，分遣精兵守其要害，以絕援兵之路。

translations.literal: (The History of Liao: At first they besieged Jin'an, dispatching elite troops to hold its vital points and cut off the roads of relief troops.)
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Liao: At first they besieged Jin'an and dispatched elite troops to hold the vital points, cutting off the roads of relief troops.)

sentences.zh: 趙延壽等皆逗留不進。）〉

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou and the others all lingered and did not advance.)
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou and the others all lingered and did not advance.)

sentences.zh: 十一月，戎王會帝於營，謂帝曰：「我三千里赴義，事須必成。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Rong king met the Emperor in camp and said to him, "I have come three thousand li to your aid; the affair must succeed."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Khitan ruler met the emperor in camp and said, "I have come three thousand li to your aid. The affair must succeed."

sentences.zh: 觀爾體貌恢廓，識量深遠，真國主也。

translations.literal: Observing your bearing, broad and imposing, and your insight, deep and far-reaching, you are truly a ruler of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Your bearing is broad and imposing, and your insight deep and far-reaching. You are truly fit to rule a state.

sentences.zh: 天命有屬，時不可失。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate has its destined recipient; the time must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate has its destined recipient. The moment must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 欲徇蕃漢群議，冊爾為天子。

translations.literal: I wish to follow the collective opinion of tribal and Chinese alike and ennoble you as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to follow the collective opinion of tribal and Chinese alike and ennoble you as Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」帝飾讓久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor made a show of declining for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made a show of declining for a long while.

sentences.zh: 既而諸軍勸請相繼，乃命築壇於晉陽城南，冊立為大晉皇帝，戎王自主解衣冠授焉。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the various armies urged him in succession, and he therefore ordered an altar built south of Jinyang city and was ennobled as Great Emperor of Jin; the Rong king himself removed his robes and cap and bestowed them upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the armies urged him in succession, and he ordered an altar built south of Jinyang. There he was ennobled as Great Emperor of Jin, and the Khitan ruler himself removed his robes and cap and bestowed them upon him.

sentences.zh: （《遼史太宗紀》：十一年冬十月甲子，封敬瑭為晉王。

translations.literal: (The Taizong Annals in the History of Liao: In the winter of the eleventh year, on the jiazi day of the tenth month, Jingtang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Taizong Annals in the History of Liao: In the winter of the eleventh year, on the jiazi day of the tenth month, Jingtang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.)

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉，冊敬瑭為大晉皇帝。）〉

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the eleventh month Jingtang was ennobled as Great Emperor of Jin.)
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the eleventh month Jingtang was ennobled as Great Emperor of Jin.)

sentences.zh: 文曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 維天顯九年，歲次丙申，十一月丙戌朔，十二日丁酉，大契丹皇帝若曰：於戲！

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianxian, the year counted as bingshen, on the dingyou day, the twelfth day of the eleventh month whose first day was bingxu, the Great Khitan Emperor spoke thus: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianxian, the year bingshen, on the dingyou day, the twelfth day of the eleventh month whose new moon was bingxu, the Great Khitan Emperor spoke thus: Alas!

sentences.zh: 元氣肇開，樹之以君；

translations.literal: When primordial energy first opened forth, a ruler was set over it;
translations.idiomatic: When primordial energy first opened forth, a ruler was set over it;

sentences.zh: 天命不恒，人輔以德。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is not constant; men are assisted by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate is not constant; men are sustained by virtue.

sentences.zh: 故商政衰而周道盛，秦德亂而漢圖昌，人事天心，古今靡異。

translations.literal: Therefore when Shang's government declined Zhou's Way flourished; when Qin's virtue fell into chaos Han's design prospered—human affairs and Heaven's heart have never differed from ancient to modern.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang's government declined, Zhou's Way flourished; when Qin's virtue fell into chaos, Han's design prospered. Human affairs and Heaven's heart have never differed from ancient times to the present.

sentences.zh: 咨爾子晉王，神鐘睿哲，天贊英雄，葉夢日以儲祥，應澄河而啟運。

translations.literal: I address you, Prince of Jin: your spirit is struck with sagely wisdom; Heaven aids your heroism; the day of the leaf-dream stored auspice; you answered the clear river and opened fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I address you, Prince of Jin: your spirit is struck with sagely wisdom, and Heaven aids your heroism. The day of the leaf-dream stored auspice, and you answered the clear river to open your fortune.

sentences.zh: 迨事數帝，歷試諸艱。

translations.literal: You have served several emperors in succession and passed through many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: You have served several emperors in succession and passed through many hardships.

sentences.zh: 武略文經，乃由天縱；

translations.literal: Military strategy and civil governance come from Heaven's gift;
translations.idiomatic: Military strategy and civil governance come from Heaven's gift;

sentences.zh: 忠規孝節，固自生知。

translations.literal: loyal counsel and filial integrity are naturally known from birth.
translations.idiomatic: loyal counsel and filial integrity are known to you from birth.

sentences.zh: 猥以眇躬，奄有北土，暨明宗之享國也，與我先哲王保奉明契，所期子孫順承，患難相濟。

translations.literal: I, unworthy in my slight person, suddenly possess the northern lands; when Mingzong enjoyed the realm, he and my former sage kings preserved and upheld a bright covenant, expecting that descendants would follow in succession and aid one another in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I, unworthy in my slight person, suddenly possess the northern lands. When Mingzong enjoyed the realm, he and my forebears preserved a bright covenant, expecting that descendants would follow in succession and aid one another in hardship.

sentences.zh: 丹書未泯，白日難欺，顧予纂承，匪敢失墜。

translations.literal: The cinnabar writing has not perished; the white sun is hard to deceive; looking to my succession, I dare not let it fall away.
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar covenant has not perished, and the white sun is hard to deceive. In my succession I dare not let it fall away.

sentences.zh: 爾惟近戚，實系本枝，所以余視爾若子，爾待予猶父也。

translations.literal: You are my close kin, truly of the same root-branch; therefore I regard you as a son, and you treat me as a father.
translations.idiomatic: You are my close kin, truly of the same root and branch. Therefore I regard you as a son, and you treat me as a father.

sentences.zh: 朕昨以獨夫從珂，本非公族，竊據寶圖，棄義忘恩，逆天暴物，誅剪骨肉，離間忠良，聽任矯諛，威虐黎獻，華夷震悚，內外崩離，知爾無辜，為彼致害。

translations.literal: I lately, because the solitary man Congke, not of the public clan, usurped the precious design, abandoned righteousness and forgot kindness, opposed Heaven and ravaged creatures, executed and cut down flesh and bone, sundered the loyal and good, listened to and entrusted flattery and sycophancy, awed and abused the black-haired people, made Chinese and barbarians tremble in fear, and caused inner and outer collapse—I knew you were innocent yet were harmed on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the solitary man Congke, not of the imperial clan, usurped the throne, abandoned righteousness and forgot kindness, opposed Heaven and ravaged the people, executed his kin, sundered the loyal and good, listened to flatterers, and awed and abused the common people until Chinese and barbarians alike trembled and the realm collapsed inward and outward. I knew you were innocent yet were harmed on his account.

sentences.zh: 敢征眾旅，來逼嚴城，雖並吞之志甚堅，而幽顯之情何負，達於聞聽，深激憤驚。

translations.literal: He dared raise hosts of troops and come to press a stern city; though his will to swallow all was very firm, how could the feelings of hidden and manifest be wronged? When this reached hearing, it deeply stirred indignation and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He dared raise armies and press a stern city. Though his will to swallow all was firm, how could the feelings of the living and the dead be wronged? When this reached my ears, it stirred deep indignation and alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃命興師，為爾除患，親提萬旅，遠殄群兇，但赴急難，罔辭艱險。

translations.literal: I therefore ordered troops raised to remove your affliction for you; personally leading ten thousand hosts, I went far to exterminate the mass of villains, coming only to urgent distress and declining no hardship or peril.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ordered troops raised to remove your affliction, personally leading ten thousand hosts far to exterminate the villains, coming only to urgent distress and declining no hardship or peril.

sentences.zh: 果見神祇助順，卿士葉謀，旗一麾而棄甲平山，鼓三作而僵屍遍野。

translations.literal: Truly we saw the spirits aid the obedient and ministers and scholars join in counsel; at one wave of the banner armor was cast aside on level hills, and at three beats of the drum stiff corpses filled the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Truly we saw the spirits aid the righteous and ministers join in counsel. At one wave of the banner armor was cast aside on the hills, and at three beats of the drum corpses filled the wilds.

sentences.zh: 雖以遂予本誌，快彼群心，將期稅駕金河，班師玉塞。

translations.literal: Though thereby my original intent was fulfilled and their multitude's hearts were gladdened, I intended soon to halt my carriage at the Golden River and withdraw the army to the Jade Barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Though thereby my original intent was fulfilled and their hearts were gladdened, I intended soon to halt at the Golden River and withdraw the army to the Jade Barrier.

sentences.zh: 矧今中原無主，四海未寧，茫茫生民，若墜塗炭。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the central plains have no ruler, the four seas are not at peace, and the vast multitude of living people are as if falling into mire and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the central plains now have no ruler, the four seas are not at peace, and the vast multitude of people are as if falling into mire and fire.

sentences.zh: 況萬幾不可以暫廢，大寶不可以久虛，拯溺救焚，當在此日。

translations.literal: Moreover, the myriad affairs cannot be briefly suspended, the great treasure cannot long stand empty; to rescue the drowning and save from burning must be on this day.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad affairs of state cannot be briefly suspended, nor the great treasure long left empty. To rescue the drowning and save those in fire must be done this day.

sentences.zh: 爾有庇民之德，格於上下；

translations.literal: You have the virtue of sheltering the people, reaching above and below;
translations.idiomatic: You have the virtue of sheltering the people, reaching above and below;

sentences.zh: 爾有戡難之勛，光於區宇；

translations.literal: you have the merit of quelling hardship, shining over the realm;
translations.idiomatic: you have the merit of quelling hardship, shining over the realm;

sentences.zh: 爾有無私之行，通乎神明；

translations.literal: you have selfless conduct, penetrating to the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: you have selfless conduct, penetrating to the spirits;

sentences.zh: 爾有不言之信，彰乎兆庶。

translations.literal: you have unspoken trustworthiness, manifest among the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: you have unspoken trustworthiness, manifest among the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 予懋乃德，嘉乃丕績。

translations.literal: I exalt your virtue and praise your great achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I exalt your virtue and praise your great achievements.

sentences.zh: 天之歷數在爾躬，是用命爾，當踐皇極。

translations.literal: Heaven's succession rests upon your person; therefore I command you to take up the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's succession rests upon your person. Therefore I command you to take up the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 仍以爾自茲並土，首建義旗，宜以國號曰晉。

translations.literal: Moreover, because you from this time in Bing land first raised the banner of righteousness, the state name should be called Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because you in Bing land first raised the banner of righteousness, the state shall be called Jin.

sentences.zh: 朕永與為父子之邦，保山河之誓。

translations.literal: I shall forever be with you as a father-and-son state, preserving the oath of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I shall forever be with you as a father-and-son state, preserving the oath of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 補百王之闕禮，行茲盛典；

translations.literal: Supplement the missing rites of the hundred kings and perform this great ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: Supplement the missing rites of the hundred kings and perform this great ceremony;

sentences.zh: 成千載之大義，遂我初心。
