translations.literal: accomplish the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplish the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.

sentences.zh: 爾其永保兆民，勉持一德，慎乃有位，允執厥中。

translations.literal: You shall forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold the center.
translations.idiomatic: Forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold the center.

sentences.zh: 亦惟無疆之休，其誡之哉！

translations.literal: May there also be boundless blessing—take this as your warning!
translations.idiomatic: May there also be boundless blessing. Take this as your warning!

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝鼓吹道從而歸。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, the Emperor returned with drums and pipes leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the emperor returned with drums and pipes leading the procession.

sentences.zh: 始梁開國之歲，即前唐天祐四年也，潞州行營使李思安奏：「壺關縣庶穰鄉鄉人伐樹，樹倒自分兩片，內有六字如左書，云『天十四載石進』。

translations.literal: In the year when Liang first founded its state, which was the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Luzhou Field Camp Commissioner Li Si'an memorialized, "In Shurang Township of Huguan County, when villagers felled a tree, the tree upon falling split of itself into two pieces; within were six characters written like left-handed script, reading 'Heaven, fourteen reigns, Shi advances.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the year Liang first founded its state, the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Luzhou field camp commissioner Li Si'an memorialized, "In Shurang Township of Huguan County, when villagers felled a tree it split of itself into two pieces. Within were six characters in left-handed script reading 'Heaven, fourteen reigns, Shi advances.'"

sentences.zh: 」梁祖令藏於武庫，然莫詳其義。

translations.literal: The Ancestor of Liang ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could explain its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Liang ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could explain its meaning.

sentences.zh: 至帝即位，識者曰：「『天』字取『四』字中兩畫加之於傍，則『丙』字也；

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, those who understood said, "From the character 'Heaven,' take the two strokes in the middle of the character 'four' and add them at the side, and you have the character 'bing';"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, those who understood said, "From the character 'Heaven,' take the two middle strokes of the character 'four' and add them at the side, and you have the character 'bing';"

sentences.zh: 『四』字去中之兩畫，加『十』字，則『申』字也。

translations.literal: from the character 'four' remove the two middle strokes and add the character 'ten,' and you have the character 'shen.'"
translations.idiomatic: from the character 'four' remove the two middle strokes and add 'ten,' and you have the character 'shen.'"

sentences.zh: 」帝即位之年乃丙申也。

translations.literal: The year in which the Emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: The year in which the emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.

sentences.zh: 又，《易》云：「晉者，進也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Book of Changes says, "Jin means advance."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Book of Changes says, "Jin means advance."

sentences.zh: 」國號大晉，皆符契焉。

translations.literal: The state name Great Jin all accorded with these tokens.
translations.idiomatic: The state name Great Jin accorded with all of these omens.

sentences.zh: 又，帝即位之前一年，歲在乙未，鄴西有柵曰李固，清、淇合流在其側。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the year before the Emperor took the throne, the year being yiwei, west of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the year before the emperor took the throne, yiwei, west of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.

sentences.zh: 柵有橋，橋下大鼠與蛇鬥，鬥及日之申，蛇不勝而死。

translations.literal: The stockade had a bridge; below the bridge a great rat and a snake fought; the fight reached the hour shen of the day, and the snake, unable to prevail, died.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade had a bridge. Below it a great rat and a snake fought until the hour shen of the day, when the snake, unable to prevail, died.

sentences.zh: 行人觀者數百，識者誌之。

translations.literal: Several hundred passersby watched; those who understood recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred passersby watched, and those who understood recorded the omen.

sentences.zh: 後唐末帝果滅於申。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Later Tang was indeed destroyed in the hour shen.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor of Later Tang was indeed destroyed at the hour shen.

sentences.zh: 又，末帝，真定常山人也，有先人舊廬，其側有古佛剎，剎有石像，忽搖動不已，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Last Emperor was a man of Zhending Changshan; he had an ancestral old dwelling, and beside it an ancient Buddhist monastery; the monastery had a stone image that suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Last Emperor came from Zhending in Changshan. Beside his ancestral dwelling stood an ancient Buddhist monastery whose stone image suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.

sentences.zh: 及重圍晉陽，帝遣心腹何福輕騎求援北蕃，蕃主自將諸部赴之。

translations.literal: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the Emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light horsemen to seek aid from the northern tribes; the tribal ruler personally led the various divisions to come.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light horsemen to seek aid from the north. The Khitan ruler personally led his divisions to come.

sentences.zh: 不以繒帛，不以珠金，若響應聲。

translations.literal: Without silks, without pearls and gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Without silks, pearls, or gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.

sentences.zh: 謂福曰：「吾已兆於夢，皆上帝命我，非我意也。」

translations.literal: He said to Fu, "I have already been foretold in a dream; all is the Supreme God's command to me, not my own intent."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Fu, "I have already been foretold in a dream. All of this is the Supreme God's command, not my own intent."

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》引《紀異錄》云：契丹主德光常晝寢，夢一神人花冠美姿容，輜梅甚盛，忽自天而下，衣白衣，佩金帶，執钅骨钅朵，有異人十二隨其後，內一黑兔入德光懷而失之。

translations.literal: (The Records of the Khitan State cites the Record of Strange Affairs: The Khitan ruler Deguang often slept by day and dreamed of a divine man with flowered crown and beautiful countenance, baggage carts and plum blossoms very abundant; suddenly he descended from Heaven, dressed in white robes, wearing a golden belt, holding a battle axe, with twelve extraordinary men following behind; among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and was lost.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Records of the Khitan State cites the Record of Strange Affairs: The Khitan ruler Deguang often slept by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, baggage carts and plum blossoms in great abundance. Suddenly he descended from Heaven in white robes, wearing a golden belt and holding a battle axe, with twelve extraordinary men following behind. Among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and vanished.)

sentences.zh: 神人語德光曰：「石郎使人喚汝，汝須去。

translations.literal: The divine man said to Deguang, "Master Shi has sent men to summon you; you must go."
translations.idiomatic: The divine man said to Deguang, "Master Shi has sent men to summon you. You must go."

sentences.zh: 」覺告其母，母忽之，不以為異。

translations.literal: Upon waking he told his mother; his mother disregarded it and did not regard it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Upon waking he told his mother, but she disregarded it and thought nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 後復夢，即前神人也，衣冠儀貌，儼然如故，曰：「石郎已使人來喚汝。

translations.literal: Later he dreamed again—it was the same divine man as before, robes, cap, bearing, and appearance all as before, who said, "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."
translations.idiomatic: Later he dreamed again. It was the same divine man as before, in the same robes, cap, and bearing, who said, "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."

sentences.zh: 」既覺而驚，復以告母。

translations.literal: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「可命筮。

translations.literal: His mother said, "You may order divination."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Order divination."

sentences.zh: 」乃召巫筮，言：「太祖從西樓來，言中國將立天王，要爾為助，爾須去。

translations.literal: He then summoned a shaman to divine, who said, "The Ancestor comes from the Western Tower, saying China will establish a Heavenly King and needs you for aid—you must go."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned a shaman, who said, "The Ancestor comes from the Western Tower, saying China will establish a Heavenly King and needs your aid. You must go."

sentences.zh: 」未浹旬，唐石敬瑭反於河東，為後唐張敬達所敗，亟遣趙瑩持表重賂，許割燕雲，求兵為援，契丹主曰：「我非為石郎興師，乃奉天帝敕使也。」）〉

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong, was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda, and urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid; the Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi; I follow the Supreme God's command.")
translations.idiomatic: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong and was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda. He urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid. The Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi. I follow the Supreme God's command.")

sentences.zh: 時援兵未至，偽將張敬達引軍逼城設柵，柵將成，必有大風暴雨，柵無以立。

translations.literal: At that time relief troops had not yet arrived; the rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops to press the city and set up stockades; whenever a stockade was about to be completed, great wind and violent rain would come, and the stockade could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops had not yet arrived. The rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops to press the city and set up stockades, but whenever a stockade was about to be completed, great wind and violent rain came and the stockade could not stand.

sentences.zh: 後築長城，城就，又為水潦所壞，城終不能合。

translations.literal: Later they built a long wall; when the wall was completed it was again destroyed by floodwaters, and the wall in the end could not be joined.
translations.idiomatic: Later they built a long wall, but when it was completed floodwaters destroyed it, and the wall in the end could not be closed.

sentences.zh: 晉陽有北宮，宮城之上有祠曰毗沙門天王，帝曾焚修默而禱之。

translations.literal: Jinyang had a Northern Palace; above the palace city was a shrine called Vaisravana Heavenly King; the Emperor once burned incense, cultivated virtue in silence, and prayed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang had a Northern Palace. Above the palace city stood a shrine to Vaisravana Heavenly King, and the emperor once burned incense in silent prayer there.

sentences.zh: 經數日，城西北正受敵處，軍候報稱，夜來有一人長丈餘，介金執殳，行於城上，久方不見。

translations.literal: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed directly, military scouts reported that in the night a man more than a zhang in height, clad in metal and holding a spear, walked upon the wall and only after a long while was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed hardest, scouts reported that in the night a man more than ten feet tall, clad in metal and holding a spear, walked upon the wall and only after a long while vanished.

sentences.zh: 帝心異之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was struck in his heart by the strangeness of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply struck by the strangeness of it.

sentences.zh: 又，牙城有僧坊曰崇福，坊之廡下西北隅有泥神，神之首忽一日有煙生，其騰郁如曲突之狀。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the citadel was a monks' quarter called Chongfu; in the northwest corner beneath its corridor was a clay spirit; one day smoke suddenly arose from the spirit's head, rising thick like a bent chimney.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the citadel was a monks' quarter called Chongfu. In the northwest corner beneath its corridor stood a clay spirit, and one day smoke suddenly arose from its head, rising thick like a bent chimney.

sentences.zh: 坊僧奔赴，以為人火所延，及俯而視之，無所有焉。

translations.literal: The monks of the quarter rushed there, thinking human fire had spread; when they bent down to look, there was nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: The monks rushed there, thinking human fire had spread, but when they bent down to look there was nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 事尋達帝，帝召僧之臘高者問焉，僧曰：「貧道見莊宗將得天下，曾有此煙。

translations.literal: The matter soon reached the Emperor; he summoned the monk of highest monastic standing and asked him; the monk said, "This humble priest saw when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm that there was once this smoke."
translations.idiomatic: The matter soon reached the emperor. He summoned the senior monk and asked him. The monk said, "This humble priest once saw the same smoke when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm."

sentences.zh: 觀此噴湧，甚於當時，兆可知矣。

translations.literal: Observing this gushing forth, it is greater than at that time; the omen can be known.
translations.idiomatic: This gushing forth is greater than at that time. The omen is clear.

sentences.zh: 」自此，日旁多有五色雲氣，如蓮芰之狀。

translations.literal: From this time onward there were often five-colored clouds beside the sun, shaped like lotus and water chestnut.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward five-colored clouds often appeared beside the sun, shaped like lotus and water chestnut.

sentences.zh: 帝召占者視之，謂曰：「此驗應誰？

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned diviners to observe them and said, "For whom is this omen fulfilled?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned diviners to observe them and asked, "For whom is this omen fulfilled?"

sentences.zh: 」占者曰：「見處為瑞，更應何人！

translations.literal: The diviners said, "Where it is seen is auspicious—for whom else could it be!"
translations.idiomatic: The diviners said, "Where it is seen is auspicious. For whom else could it be!"

sentences.zh: 」又，帝每詰旦使慰撫守陴者，率以為常。

translations.literal: Moreover, every dawn the Emperor sent men to comfort those guarding the battlements, making this his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every dawn the emperor sent men to comfort those guarding the battlements, making this his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 忽一夕已暝，城上有號令之聲，聲不絕者三。

translations.literal: Suddenly one evening after dark, upon the wall came the sound of commands, the sound continuing three times without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly one evening after dark, commands were heard upon the wall three times without cease.

sentences.zh: 帝使人問之，將吏云：「從上傳來者。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent men to inquire; the officers said, "They come transmitted from above."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to inquire. The officers said, "They come from above."

sentences.zh: 」皆知神助。

translations.literal: All knew it was divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: All knew it was divine aid.

sentences.zh: 時城中復有數家井泉，暴溢不止。

translations.literal: At that time within the city several households' wells and springs burst forth without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: At that time several wells and springs within the city burst forth without stopping.

sentences.zh: 及蕃軍大至，合勢破之，末帝之眾，似拉朽焉。

translations.literal: When the tribal army arrived in great force and joined strength to break them, the Last Emperor's host was like pulling rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal army arrived in great force and joined in the attack, the Last Emperor's host collapsed like rotten wood.

sentences.zh: 斯天運使然，非人力也。

translations.literal: This was Heaven's course making it so, not human power.
translations.idiomatic: This was Heaven's course at work, not human power.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝言於契丹主，願以雁門已北及幽州之地為戎王壽，仍約歲輸帛三十萬，戎王許之。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor said to the Khitan ruler that he wished to give the lands north of Yanmen and the region of Youzhou as a gift for the Rong king's longevity, and also agreed to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk annually; the Rong king assented.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor told the Khitan ruler that he wished to give the lands north of Yanmen and the region of Youzhou as a gift for his longevity, and also agreed to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk annually. The Khitan ruler assented.
